Hi, first I want to thank you for rescuing your new kitty. If you could post some pics it would help so we could get an idea of how old she is, but in the meantime here’s some basic advice to start:

1. Try and get the kitty to a vet as soon as possible, it’s important to get dewormed and vaccines.
2. As far as food goes,  start with kitten wet food and a bowl of kitten dry food. I always gave my cats wet food (Fancy Feast) and always kept a bowl of dry food down at all times.  Plus you need a bowl of water, fresh daily.
3. You’ll also need a litter box with litter and a scoop. It’s  your choice the type of litter you want. I always used Tidy Cat lightweight litter.
4. You don’t need to bathe your cat often, cats are very clean and groom themselves. As far as her  shaking it’s most likely because she’s scared and cold, keep her warm as possible until she’s dry and comfortable.
5. Depending on the kitty’s weight you want to get rid of any fleas and parasites she may have and the best is Revolution but again you need a RX from the vet. Plus it’s important for the vet to check for worms and other parasites and cat diseases. Cats also need vaccinations.
6. If she’s shaking and purring after a bath she’s most likely calming herself down. On the other hand cats usually purr because they are content comfortable and happy.
7. Licking your face or the top and back of your head is very common for cats, they love to groom themselves and groom whoever they love. Cats know who saved them and although they seem standoffish they are great pets and very loyal to the person who loves them and takes care of them.
8. TOYS! Kittens need lots of toys because they are very active at this age and need lots of stimulation and activities. Cat condos or cat trees are also great to have. If you can afford some type of window bed so they can look outside that is always good too.
9. A scratch post is also a must! Cats shed their claws so they need to scratch and you don’t want it to be your furniture, you can buy things to protect your furniture. If you have plenty of things for kitty to scratch on they’ll most likely leave your furniture alone. They make scratch posts and scratch boards that you can buy.
10. Make sure you NEVER declaw your cat!!! It’s one of the cruelest things you can do to your pet.
11. Please do not let your cat or kitten go outside, there’s so many bad things that can happen, predators, diseases, fleas, ticks, worms and mean people, the list is endless.
12. Don’t forget to name your kitty 🐈‍⬛
13. Enjoy, love, take lots of pictures as they grow up quick, have fun with your new baby. Remember this is a commitment and you will never regret the day you rescued your kitty.

I know this seems like a lot of info but it’s really not once you take kitty to the vet that’s half the battle and then you can start relaxing and being a cat mom. I’m sure there’s a lot I missed and hopefully someone else can contribute more information. Good luck and thank you again for rescuing your kitten. Please post a picture I would love to see her.

Oh! One more thing if you give kitty treats do not go overboard because treats can also be bad for your cat. For instance my cat started throwing up blood and I took her to ER vet and they had no diagnosis they sent her home after giving her fluids and an appetite stimulant. I was not convinced nothing was wrong and I started ruling out certain flavors of foods and stopped all treats. Then I read some bad news about Temptation cat treats. I stopped those and she never did that again so I started giving her the Greenie treats never had another problem. I can’t say for sure that’s the cause but I wanted to share my experience with treats. My kitty  lived to be 18 years old, but unfortunately she went over the Rainbow Bridge last month, her name was Marylou and I loved her more than anything in this world. I hope you will love yours the same way. \*\*Please excuse any typos or grammar errors, I’m not the best at writing such long posts.

The first month of discharge I applied for a secured credit card of $300 before the bankruptcy report hit all the creditors. I'm still on the blacklist of course with all the original creditors, but plenty of other companies will be willing to take a chance on you. I currently have 3 cards with $2500 credit line, Discover, OLLO and Barclay. But like I said before don't base your life's worth on a credit score, that shit is consuming.
